note: ser is what something IS; estar is how or where it is right now
note_back: estar is the state or place; ser is the identity

note: saber is facts and skills: sé la respuesta, sé nadar
note_back: conocer is people and places you are acquainted with: conozco a Ana

note: pedir asks FOR a thing: pido un café
note_back: preguntar asks a question: pregunto dónde está

note: tomar is taking hold of or drinking it
note_back: llevar is carrying it with you somewhere

note: llevar carries away from where you are
note_back: traer brings toward where you are

note: ir goes away from the speaker

note_back: devolver is giving a thing back

note: dejar leaves a thing or person behind: dejé las llaves
note_back: salir is going out of a place: salí de casa

note: jugar plays a game or sport
note_back: tocar plays an instrument (and means to touch)

note: ver is seeing, whether you meant to or not
note_back: mirar is looking at on purpose

note: oír is hearing, whether you meant to or not
decir says words to someone: me dijo que sí
note_back: hablar is speaking or talking: hablo español
contar tells a story or recounts it
pasar spends time: pasé dos horas allí
ahorrar saves up money or effort

note: conseguir gets hold of a thing
pensar is the act of thinking it over
note_back: creer is holding an opinion or believing it

note: esperar is both waiting and hoping; context decides
false friend: realizar is to carry out, not to realise
note_back: hacer is the everyday do or make

note: false friend: asistir is to attend, not to assist
false friend: soportar is to put up with
note_back: apoyar is to support a person or an idea
probar is to try it out or taste it
parecerse looks like: se parece a su padre

note: haber is the helper for perfect tenses, and hay = there is
note_back: tener is to have as a possession
hacerse becomes, through your own doing
ponerse puts clothes on, or turns a sudden mood

note: sacar takes something out of somewhere
note_back: quitar removes or takes away from someone

note: tomar is the everyday word for drinking
note_back: beber is to drink, slightly more formal

note: importar is to matter to you
note_back: interesar is to be interesting to you

note: gustar is to be pleasing: me gusta
note_back: querer is to want, or to love a person

note: querer is the ordinary love you say out loud
note_back: amar is the weightier, more literary love

note: deber + infinitive is a moral should
note_back: tener que + infinitive is a practical have to

note: poder is can as in allowed or able right now
note_back: saber is can as in knows how
recordar remembers, and also reminds someone

note: acordar is to agree on something
note_back: acordarse de is to remember it
irse is leaving, with no destination needed
comenzar is the same, a touch more formal

note: acabar finishes, and acabar de means to have just done
seguir keeps on, and also follows
andar is to go about, and works for machines too
regresar returns, common in the Americas
quedar is to be left, to arrange to meet, or how clothes fit
casar marries two people, as the official does
perder loses a thing or a game
note_back: perderse is getting lost, or missing out on

note: up: subir a go up, climb, get on, raise
note_back: down: bajar go down, get off, lower
